rows.best_lead_title: A study of superconductivity in lead-bismuth alloys using electron tunneling techniques (1965)
rows.reason: Pb dissolves in Bi to well under 1 at.%, so a bulk Bi0.95Pb0.05 sample is two-phase: Bi plus the Pb-Bi epsilon phase. Any transition would come from the epsilon precipitates, and two-phase samples do not count under the rule. The only composition-specific lead is about films, and it says Bi films with small amounts of Pb do not superconduct above 1 K. The other leads cover Pb-rich alloys, films under quantum confinement or high pressure. Nothing reports single-phase bulk superconductivity near 95 at.% Bi.

rows.best_lead_title: Heat Transport in Lead-Bismuth Alloys (J. L. Olsen, Proc. Phys. Soc. A 65, 1952)
rows.reason: Pb with 7.5 at.% Bi sits inside the single-phase fcc Pb solid solution, which extends to roughly 20 at.% Bi. Bulk alloys in this range are textbook strong-coupling superconductors with Tc of about 7.2-7.5 K. Olsen's abstract reports a bulk series of Pb-Bi alloys measured in both the superconducting and the normal state. Two more full-text targets have the Tc-versus-composition data needed to check the 2 at.% bracket: Malseed and Rachinger, 'Superconductivity in the lead-bismuth system' (Scripta Met. 1969, 10.1016/0036-9748(69)90270-1), and Gamari-Seale and Coles 1965 on dilute Pb alloys (10.1088/0370-1328/86/6/305). Gandhi et al. 2017 (10.1088/1361-6668/aa83d7) is a further source. The IOP PDFs were blocked from this session (captcha/403), so the sample lists have not been read yet.

rows.best_lead_title: Niobium's Special Role (C&EN news item, 1970)
rows.reason: The composition is Nb2.45(Al0.7Ge0.3). The only lead is a news item about Nb0.79(Al0.75Ge0.25)0.21 at about 21 K. That composition is 8 at.% away in Nb, so it is neither this composition nor a bracketing series. At 71 at.% Nb a bulk Nb-Al-Ge sample would normally be two-phase (A15 plus sigma). Even if it showed A15 superconductivity, it could not meet the single-phase rule. The label looks physically odd, but these leads cannot correct it.

rows.best_lead_title: Superconductivity and magnetic order in La-Ce alloys (J. Wollan, Ames Lab report, 1970)
rows.reason: The report measured resistivity from 0.06 to 20 K on La with 0.2, 1.0, 2.0, 3.2 and 4.0 wt.% Ce. Ce and La have almost the same atomic mass, so 4.0 wt.% Ce is about 3.97 at.%, within 0.15 at.% of this composition. The abstract says Tc falls as Ce is added, more slowly than Abrikosov-Gor'kov theory predicts. It does not say whether the 4 wt.% sample still superconducts above 0.06 K. Ce in La is a strong magnetic (Kondo) pair breaker, so the sample may be normal, which would mean the label is correct. The report's Tc table settles it. The OSTI PDF was blocked by the proxy (403). The 1967 PRL tunneling study is on films and does not count.

rows.best_lead_title: Shu et al., Correlated electron state in Ce1-xYbxCoIn5 stabilized by cooperative valence fluctuations (PRL 106, 156403, 2011); the JSON lead is the matching 2009 UCSD thesis
rows.reason: The composition is Ce0.225Yb0.775CoIn5, nominal x of about 0.775. The leads are Maple-group theses covering the full Yb range. Jang et al. (arXiv 1407.6725) say superconductivity persists to nominal x of about 0.8, with Tc measured from x=0 to 0.7 and falling linearly from 2.3 K. They also find the actual Yb content is only about x/3 up to x of about 0.5, and phase separation sets in above about 0.8. Capan et al. EPL 2010 (arXiv 0912.0046, Table 1) report Tc = 0.77 K at nominal x = 0.8, but with a small, broad specific-heat jump, so not bulk. They also say effective Yb never reached 0.3 and that batches with nominal x of 0.7 or more grew mostly pure YbCoIn5. Superconductivity is reported near this nominal composition, but the bulk, single-phase and actual-composition conditions look likely to fail. A sceptical verifier would probably refute this one, so it has a low prior.

rows.best_lead_title: Deep and resonance states in A IV B VI semiconductors (1985)
rows.reason: The only lead is a review of IV-VI semiconductor impurity states, which is irrelevant. Bi-Ge is a simple eutectic with no intermediate compound and negligible mutual solubility, so Bi2Ge is not a bulk ambient-pressure phase. No lead reports superconductivity here.

rows.best_lead_title: Superconductivity in Hf5Sb3-xRux (2015)
rows.reason: The compound is HfRu with the CsCl structure. The leads are a different compound (Hf5Sb3-xRux, where Ru is a minor dopant) and a 1976 review of lattice instabilities that does not mention HfRu. A FastTrack search found nothing on superconductivity in HfRu. Two source reports agree it is not a superconductor.

rows.best_lead_title: Superconductivity in the Alloy System Cadmium-Mercury and the Effect of Ordering upon Superconductivity (Claeson, Luo, Merriam, 1966)
rows.reason: Tc was measured over the complete Cd-Hg composition range, so the paper may have a sample at 90 at.% Hg. But the abstract's own phase boundaries put that composition in the two-phase Hg(Cd) plus omega field at 193 K: Cd solubility in Hg is 1.5 at.%, and the omega phase ends at 88±1 at.% Hg. That fails the single-phase rule unless the full text shows this sample as single-phase omega. Cycle 2 reached the same outcome for Cd0.05Hg0.95 from this paper: not confirmed, and the APS full text was blocked. Low prior.

rows.best_lead_title: Synthesis and superconductivity in yttrium-cerium hydrides at high pressures (2024)
rows.reason: The leads are Y-Ce hydrides made and measured at more than 100 GPa, plus a specific-heat study of CeRu2 alloys. All are irrelevant: hydrides and pressure do not count. Yttrium does not superconduct at ambient pressure, and Ce is a magnetic impurity. No lead reports ambient-pressure bulk superconductivity in Y-1.7 at.% Ce.

rows.best_lead_title: Properties of some superconductors (1940)
rows.reason: The only lead covers elemental Al, Ga, Th, Zn, Ti, Mo and U. It says nothing about a Ti-Mo-Ga alloy or a Ti2MoGa compound. Two source reports label this composition non-superconducting, and no lead contradicts them.

rows.best_lead_title: Superconductivity in the Palladium-Hydrogen System (1975)
rows.reason: Every superconductivity report in the leads concerns something other than bulk Pd metal: He-ion-irradiated Pd films, Pd hydride, deuteride or tritide, or Pd compounds such as YPd2B2C and the Pd2ZrAl Heusler alloys. The 1975 PRL explains why Pd metal itself does not superconduct (large Coulomb pseudopotential). Three source reports agree it is not a superconductor.

rows.best_lead_title: Synthesis of molecular metallic barium superhydride: pseudocubic BaH12 (2021)
rows.reason: The composition is essentially BaB6 (Ba 0.143). The only lead is BaH12 synthesized at 75-173 GPa, which is an irrelevant hydride under pressure. Nothing on Ba-B superconductivity was found.

rows.best_lead_title: Electronic properties, superconductivity and stability of the ordered alloys of the Ti-Rh, Zr-Rh and Hf-Rh isoelectronic systems (Kuentzler & Waterstrat, 1988)
rows.reason: The composition is Ti2Rh. The JSON lead, 'Superconductivity and specific heat of titanium-rhodium alloys' (1968), is on this system but has no DOI or abstract. It probably covers the Ti-rich bcc alloys. A FastTrack search found two further papers on this system, both paywalled with no abstract: Raub and Andersen 1963 on Ti- and Zr-Rh alloys (10.1007/bf01375398), and Kuentzler and Waterstrat 1988 on the ordered Ti-Rh compounds. One of these could state Tc, or its absence, for Ti2Rh. Three source reports agree it is not a superconductor, so the prior is low.

rows.best_lead_title: Evidence for superconductivity at Tc=12 K in oxygen-deficient MoO2-delta (2014)
rows.reason: The leads are a 12 K signal attributed to a roughly 4 wt.% MoO2-delta impurity in a molybdenum arsenide sample, at about 33 at.% Mo and not bulk, and Mo-doped Tl cuprates. Neither concerns a Mo5O2 (Mo 71 at.%) composition. No lead reports superconductivity here.

rows.best_lead_title: Superconductivity with Tc of 116 K discovered in antimony polyhydrides (2023)
rows.reason: The leads are an Sb polyhydride at 184 GPa, a theory paper on pnictogen hydrides under pressure, and Sb-substituted NdO0.7F0.3BiS2. All are irrelevant: hydrides, pressure, theory and other compounds. Nothing concerns an Sb-S solid at SbS3 stoichiometry at ambient pressure.

rows.best_lead_title: Physical properties of noncentrosymmetric tungsten and molybdenum aluminides (Peets et al., 2018; arXiv 1807.03476)
rows.reason: The composition is Al12Mo. The lead's full text (arXiv 1807.03476) covers Al12Mo single crystals. Specific heat shows no phase transition down to about 0.3 K (Fig. 4b, Table IV), and magnetization shows no superconducting signal above 1.8 K. Resistivity was not measured because the crystals were too small. The lead therefore supports the non-superconductor label.
